# /family

The wall itself: the grid of everyone's drawing for a prompt, day by day. Four
of the app's nine flows end here, more journeys than any other screen absorbs
([screen-flow-inventory.md](/design/screen-flow-inventory) calls it "the
landing point for four different journeys"). It also doubles as the personal
archive view when `channelId` is the caller's own archive channel, and it is
where a wall's multi-select starts, the only door into `/compose`.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/family` |
| Router file | `app/family.tsx` |
| Flows | F3 Invite and join, F4 Daily create and submit, F5 Wall browsing and composition, F7 Wall creation and administration (see [screen-flow-inventory.md](/design/screen-flow-inventory)) |
| Position in flow | landing point for F3/F4, browsing home for F5, one entry point for F7 |
| Data calls | five reads (roster, channel days, day members, wall prompts, archive) and two writes (heart a response, submit a text reflection) |
| Shared surface | `BottomNav`; `WallMemberCard`/`WallMemberAvatarRow`, also on `/wall/[id]/members` |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

Both tiles show the screen's real interface. This matters because the
inventory's Finding 2 says the `/family` tile "reads 'Pick a family wall from
Home.' The route is reached but no wall is in context." That was true of the
capture the inventory read, at `c68de8d` on `main`. It is not true of tile 18
above, captured at `72c3ab8`: the empty-state string only exists in the source
at `app/family.tsx:962-968`, gated on `!channelId`, and tile 18 shows a wall
with a `channelId` in context instead. The newer capture branch seeds a wall
the same way it seeds an onboarding draft (see
[note 1 on the F2 workflow page](/prototype/workflows/f2-first-run-onboarding)).
So the single most consequential missing capture the inventory flagged is no
longer missing, on this branch; `c68de8d`'s empty-state tile is stale, not a
live problem, until `72c3ab8` merges.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|-----------------|
| See today's prompt and everyone's drawing for it, once unlocked | `app/family.tsx:1081-1090`, grid at `:364-433` |
| Draw to unlock a locked today | `app/family.tsx:340-358` |
| Leave a text-only reflection instead of drawing, on a locked past day | `ReflectionInput`, `app/family.tsx:106-161`, mounted at `:360-362` |
| Heart a response directly from the grid, no navigation | `heartResponse`, `app/family.tsx:752-760`, tile control inside `WallMemberCard` |
| Open a response's full view | `app/family.tsx:381-386`, navigates to `/response/[id]` |
| Toggle multi-select mode | `app/family.tsx:898-916` |
| Select drawings as compose sources while in multi-select | `toggleComposeSource`/`handleToggleSelect`, `app/family.tsx:768-803` |
| Combine selected drawings, once at least two are picked | `app/family.tsx:918-933`, disabled while `composeSources.length < 2` |
| Pick prompts from a game pack, creator only | `app/family.tsx:1092-1105`, navigates to `/wall/[id]/prompt-packs` |
| Draw against an injected pack prompt nobody has answered yet | `app/family.tsx:1120-1152` |
| Browse the personal archive gallery, when the channel is the archive | `app/family.tsx:985-1044` |

Two things worth stating as gates rather than omissions. First, the add-member
entry point is not missing by accident: a comment at `app/family.tsx:1107-1111`
records that it was "removed from here. Adding a member is rare, and this
button sat on a screen people use every day for a once-in-a-while action.
It's still reachable from Settings." That matches the inventory's F7
section, which names `app/settings.tsx:164` as the one remaining call site.
Second, the game-pack entry is creator-gated: `isWallCreator` guards the
button at `app/family.tsx:1092`, computed by comparing the roster's
`createdBy` against the current user (`app/family.tsx:481-482`). The comment
at `:476-480` calls this "a courtesy gate only" -- the server enforces the
real 403 on the write, this only hides the button for a non-creator.

## Data calls

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `getChannelRoster(channelId)` | `GET /channels/{id}/roster` | `channel-roster.ts` |
| `listChannelDays(channelId)` | `GET /channels/{id}/days` | `channel-days.ts` |
| `getChannelMembers` (via `useFamilyStore.loadDays`) | `GET /channels/{id}/members` | `channel-members.ts` |
| `addReaction(channelId, promptId, responseId, emoji)` | `POST /channels/{id}/responses/{id}/reactions` | `reaction-add.ts` |
| `submit({ promptId, channelIds, text })` | `POST /submit` | not traced further here; see the reflection call site below |

Handler paths are relative to `backend/lambda/handlers/`.

The roster call is the authoritative membership source and the only one that
reflects a removal immediately; the screen's own comment at
`app/family.tsx:483-487` says so explicitly. `getChannelMembers` is not called
directly by the screen; it is called by `useFamilyStore`'s `loadDays`
(imported at `app/family.tsx:36`), per that store's own doc comment referenced
at `app/family.tsx:439-443`. Hearting a response calls `reactToResponse` off
`useFamilyStore` (`app/family.tsx:757`), which wraps `addReaction`. The
text-only reflection path calls `dataClient.submit` directly from
`ReflectionInput` (`app/family.tsx:119`), the same endpoint the drawing submit
flow uses.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** `channelId` from route params (`app/family.tsx:447`).
Roster, channel days, wall prompts, and (for today) the day's members, all
fetched in effects keyed on `channelId` (`app/family.tsx:539-548`,
`:600-604`, `:627-631`). The personal archive gallery instead loads every
response for every prompt the archive has ever drawn (`app/family.tsx:617-622`).

**Writes on mount.** None to the API beyond the reads above; `usePromptStore`
and `useWallsStore` also load (`app/family.tsx:499-505`).

**Writes on focus.** Roster, channel days, and today's day reload on every
focus, not just mount (`app/family.tsx:638-659`), so returning from `/draw` or
from the members screen shows current state rather than a stale cache. The
comment at `:633-637` states the reason directly.

**Writes on exit.** None from this screen's own state; selecting drawings
writes into `useComposeStore` (`toggleSource`, `app/family.tsx:785`), which
`/compose` then reads.

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### The inventory's empty-state finding is already out of date

Finding 2 is accurate about the capture it read and inaccurate about the one
committed here. That is worth flagging as a process point, not just a content
one: a finding cited against one capture generation can silently go stale the
moment a newer capture lands, the same failure mode the F2 workflow page's
note 1 already caught for the onboarding tiles. Whatever fixes that drift for
onboarding should cover `/family` too.

### One screen, two very different interfaces

The archive branch (`isArchive`, `app/family.tsx:985-1044`) and the group-wall
branch (`app/family.tsx:1046-1161`) share almost nothing but the route and the
bottom nav: different data source, different empty state, different tile
component. That is a reasonable way to have built a POC fast, but it means
"the family screen" is really two screens wearing one file, and any future
split should be planned rather than discovered.

### The compose entry point is easy to miss

Multi-select is a small menu-icon toggle in the header (`app/family.tsx:898-916`),
with no label and no onboarding of its own. It is the only door to `/compose`
in the whole app (per the inventory), so a person who never taps that icon
never finds composition at all. Worth deciding whether that is an acceptable
discoverability trade for a POC before treating composition as shipped-feature
complete.
